claim: Meta-analysis of 56 studies: human grey-matter electrical conductivity has a weighted mean of 0.47 S/m (raw mean 0.5981 S/m, SD 0.2392, min 0.06, max 2.47; 66 values from 16 studies, 153 participants), measured at 0-1005 Hz.

source.authors: McCann H, Pisano G, Beltrachini L
source.title: Variation in Reported Human Head Tissue Electrical Conductivity Values

evidence_location: Abstract (weighted means) and Table 3 'Descriptive statistics for each tissue type', row GM
notes: Full text retrieved from PMC6708046 via the NCBI BioC API. Table 3 weighted mean for GM is 0.4660 S/m, rounded to 0.47 S/m in the abstract. Note: this is NOT the ~0.33 S/m often quoted; frequency range 0-1005 Hz per Results 3.2 (bioRxiv version).

claim: Recommended weighted-average head-tissue conductivities from the same meta-analysis: scalp 0.41 S/m, whole skull 0.02 S/m, CSF 1.71 S/m, grey matter 0.47 S/m, white matter 0.22 S/m, brain-to-skull conductivity ratio 50.4.

source.authors: McCann H, Pisano G, Beltrachini L
source.title: Variation in Reported Human Head Tissue Electrical Conductivity Values

quote: 0.41 S/m for the scalp, 0.02 S/m for the whole skull ... 0.47 S/m for the grey matter
notes: Abstract text seen via Europe PMC API (PMID 31054104). Table 3 gives whole-skull weighted mean 0.0160 S/m (abstract rounds to 0.02).

claim: In vivo measurements in monkey primary visual cortex show the cortical impedance spectrum is independent of frequency, homogeneous and tangentially isotropic within grey matter, and is predicted by assuming a purely resistive conductor (i.e., ohmic, no capacitive filtering at LFP/EEG frequencies).

source.authors: Logothetis NK, Kayser C, Oeltermann A
source.title: In vivo measurement of cortical impedance spectrum in monkeys: implications for signal propagation

quote: impedance is independent of frequency, is homogeneous and tangentially isotropic within gray matter
notes: Only the abstract was readable (Cell Press full text could not be fetched). The numeric conductivity/resistivity values and the measured frequency range reported in the full text were NOT verified.

claim: Quasistatic approximation is valid for brain signals: with conductivity 0.3 S/m (value for brain tissue), permittivity 1e5 eps0 and f = 100 Hz, the ratio of capacitive to ohmic current 2*pi*f*eps/sigma = 2e-3 << 1, so dE/dt and dB/dt source terms can be ignored.

source.authors: Hämäläinen M, Hari R, Ilmoniemi RJ, Knuutila J, Lounasmaa OV
source.title: Magnetoencephalography—theory, instrumentation, and applications to noninvasive studies of the working human brain

evidence_location: Section III.A 'Quasistatic approximation', p. 426 (section starts p. 425)
quote: f = 100 Hz, we find 2 pi f eps/sigma = 2 x 10^-3 << 1
notes: Full-text PDF (Aalto University open repository copy) read with pdftotext. Also supplies the textbook-style sigma = 0.3 S/m figure for brain tissue that Nunez & Srinivasan use (Nunez & Srinivasan itself was not fetched).

claim: Plonsey & Heppner (1967) set out the conditions under which the time-varying electromagnetic field problem in electrophysiological systems reduces to the conventional quasistatic problem, evaluated for typical physiological parameters.

source.authors: Plonsey R, Heppner DB
source.title: Considerations of quasi-stationarity in electrophysiological systems

quote: can be reduced to the conventional quasistatic problem are summarized. These conditions are discussed for typical physiological parameters.
notes: Abstract only; the paper's numeric thresholds (frequency, sigma, eps, wavelength) are paywalled and were not seen. Use t1-04 (Hämäläinen) and t1-03 (Logothetis) for the numbers.

claim: Potential of a point current source (monopole) of magnitude I0 in an infinite homogeneous conductor of conductivity sigma: Phi = I0 / (4 pi sigma r); potential falls as 1/r.

source.authors: Malmivuo J, Plonsey R
source.title: Bioelectromagnetism: Principles and Applications of Bioelectric and Biomagnetic Fields

evidence_location: Chapter 8, Section 8.2.1 'Monopole', Equation 8.7 (image eq/e0807.gif) and following text
quote: the potential magnitude is inversely proportional to the radius (with the origin at the monopole source)
notes: Equation image e0807.gif downloaded from bem.fi and read visually: Phi = I0/(4 pi sigma r).

claim: Potential of a current dipole of moment p in an infinite homogeneous conductor: Phi_d = p cos(theta) / (4 pi sigma r^2); the dipole field varies as 1/r^2 whereas the monopole field varies as 1/r.

source.authors: Malmivuo J, Plonsey R
source.title: Bioelectromagnetism: Principles and Applications of Bioelectric and Biomagnetic Fields

evidence_location: Chapter 8, Section 8.2.2 'Dipole', Equation 8.15 (image eq/e0815.gif) and the comparison sentence that follows it
quote: the dipole field varies as (1/r)^2 whereas the monopole field varies as (1/r)
notes: Equation image e0815.gif read visually: Phi_d = p cos(theta)/(4 pi sigma r^2), theta = polar (colatitude) angle; p = I0*d.

claim: In rat hippocampal CA1 in vivo, extracellular spikes recorded within 50 um of the soma are >= 60 uV (the largest observed units were ~600 uV), and at distances > 140 um no spike could be distinguished from background noise even with spike-triggered averaging.

source.authors: Henze DA, Borhegyi Z, Csicsvari J, Mamiya A, Harris KD, Buzsáki G
source.title: Intracellular features predicted by extracellular recordings in the hippocampus in vivo

quote: the amplitude of the spikes <50 um from the tetrode is >=60 uV and is therefore detectable
notes: Full-text PDF copy (typeset.io mirror of the J Neurophysiol article) read with pdftotext. Second supporting sentence: 'At extracellular distances >140 um from the soma (Fig. 6C), no extracellular spike activity could be distinguished from the background noise'.

claim: A single tetrode in CA1 is within 140 um of ~1,000 (calculated 1,108) neurons; 60-100 of these should produce spikes large enough (>60 uV, i.e. within ~50 um) to be detected and sorted, versus ~6 units typically detected per tetrode.

source.authors: Henze DA, Borhegyi Z, Csicsvari J, Mamiya A, Harris KD, Buzsáki G
source.title: Intracellular features predicted by extracellular recordings in the hippocampus in vivo

quote: extracellular spikes can be revealed as far as 140 um from the cell body
notes: Abstract: 'a tetrode in hippocampal area CA1 theoretically should be able to record electrical signals from approximately 1,000 neurons. Of these, 60-100 neurons should generate spikes of sufficient amplitude'.

claim: Modeled extracellular spike amplitude decays with distance r from the soma as 1/r^n with 1 <= n <= 2 close to the soma and n >= 2 far away, and spikes are low-pass filtered (spike width increases) with increasing distance.

source.authors: Pettersen KH, Einevoll GT
source.title: Amplitude variability and extracellular low-pass filtering of neuronal spikes

quote: decaying as 1/r(n) with 1 <= n <= 2 close to soma and n >= 2 far away
notes: Abstract obtained via Europe PMC REST API (PMC2186261). Amplitude is 'approximately proportional to the sum of the dendritic cross-sectional areas of all dendritic branches connected to the soma'. DOI not displayed in the API record; taken from the article's standard citation.

claim: Modeled spatial reach of the LFP: for uncorrelated synaptic activity the LFP represents cells within a radius of a few hundred micrometres; for correlated activity the generating region is set by the spatial extent of the correlated activity (reach can be much larger).

source.authors: Lindén H, Tetzlaff T, Potjans TC, Pettersen KH, Grün S, Diesmann M, Einevoll GT
source.title: Modeling the spatial reach of the LFP

quote: For uncorrelated activity, the LFP represents cells in a small region (within a radius of a few hundred micrometers)
notes: Abstract verified; the specific figure (~200 um) given in the full text was not seen (Cell Press full text not fetchable). DOI not displayed on fetched page (from memory). Companion CNS*2011 abstract (PMC3240187) states for correlated input 'the LFP reach is only limited by the size of the region of correlated sources'.

claim: Current dipole moment of single neocortical neurons (realistic 3-D models): layer V pyramidal spikes -0.78 to 2.97 pA·m (burst envelope -0.41 to -0.90 pA·m); layer II/III pyramidal spike 0.47 and envelope -0.29 pA·m; layer IV spiny stellate 0.27 pA·m; layer III aspiny stellate 0.06 pA·m.

source.authors: Murakami S, Okada Y
source.title: Contributions of principal neocortical neurons to magnetoencephalography and electroencephalography signals

quote: spikes produced by the layer V pyramidal cells (n = 4) varied between -0.78 and 2.97 pA m
notes: Abstract via Europe PMC API (PMID 16613883). Positive = current toward the pia.

claim: Burst discharges of pyramidal cells may become detectable with MEG and EEG when 10,000-50,000 cells are synchronously active (i.e., roughly 0.3-1 pA·m per cell summing to ~10 nA·m).

source.authors: Murakami S, Okada Y
source.title: Contributions of principal neocortical neurons to magnetoencephalography and electroencephalography signals

quote: may be detectable with MEG and EEG when 10 000-50 000 cells are synchronously active
notes: The parenthetical per-cell arithmetic is mine, not the paper's. The 10 nA·m detectability criterion is from Hämäläinen 1993 (t1-14).

claim: A typical current-dipole strength explaining measured MEG fields, caused by the synchronous activity of probably tens of thousands of neurons, is 10 nA·m.

source.authors: Hämäläinen M, Hari R, Ilmoniemi RJ, Knuutila J, Lounasmaa OV
source.title: Magnetoencephalography—theory, instrumentation, and applications to noninvasive studies of the working human brain

evidence_location: Section I.C (current dipole model), p. 418; repeated p. 424
quote: caused by the synchronous activity of probably tens of thousands of neurons, is 10 nA m
notes: Full-text PDF (Aalto open repository). p. 424 adds: 'current-dipole moments required to explain the measured magnetic-field strengths outside the head are on the order of 10 nAm'.

claim: A single postsynaptic potential (PSP) produces a current dipole of about 20 fA·m, so roughly a million synapses must be simultaneously active to produce a typical 10 nA·m evoked-response dipole.

source.authors: Hämäläinen M, Hari R, Ilmoniemi RJ, Knuutila J, Lounasmaa OV
source.title: Magnetoencephalography—theory, instrumentation, and applications to noninvasive studies of the working human brain

quote: Q = 20 fA m for a single PSP ... about a million synapses must be simultaneously active
notes: Computed in the paper from intracellular conductivity, dendrite diameter and a 25 mV PSP. Same page: ~10^5 pyramidal cells per mm^2 of cortex and thousands of synapses per neuron.

claim: An action potential in an unmyelinated cortical axon (v = 1 m/s) is approximated by two opposite current dipoles of ~100 fA·m separated by ~1 mm, i.e. a quadrupole whose field falls off as 1/r^3, faster than the 1/r^2 dipolar field of synaptic currents.
units: fA·m (each dipole of the AP quadrupole)

source.authors: Hämäläinen M, Hari R, Ilmoniemi RJ, Knuutila J, Lounasmaa OV
source.title: Magnetoencephalography—theory, instrumentation, and applications to noninvasive studies of the working human brain

quote: in an unmyelinated cortical axon where v = 1 m/s; the magnitude of each dipole is about 100 fAm
notes: Explains why synaptic (dipolar) currents, not spikes, dominate EEG/MEG at a distance.

claim: Unitary EPSPs between thick-tufted layer 5 pyramidal neurons (young rat somatosensory cortex) have mean peak amplitude 1.3 +/- 1.1 mV (range 0.15-5.5 mV) with an inferred quantal peak conductance of 1.5-5.5 nS (mean 3 nS); a direct unitary EPSC in pA is not reported.

source.authors: Markram H, Lübke J, Frotscher M, Roth A, Sakmann B
source.title: Physiology and anatomy of synaptic connections between thick tufted pyramidal neurones in the developing rat neocortex

quote: mean peak amplitude ranging from 0.15 to 5.5 mV in different connections with a mean of 1.3 +/- 1.1 mV
notes: Abstract via Europe PMC API. Derived (NOT from the paper): 3 nS x ~60 mV driving force ~ 180 pA per quantal event; 4-8 contacts per connection. A primary pA-scale EPSC measurement was not located within budget.

claim: Neuropixels probes achieve an action-potential-band noise floor of ~5 uV rms (Extended Data Table 1: 5.5-6.6 uV rms depending on configuration) and ~9 uV rms in the LFP band, with low-impedance TiN sites.

source.authors: Jun JJ, Steinmetz NA, Siegle JH, et al.
source.title: Fully integrated silicon probes for high-density recording of neural activity

evidence_location: Main text (Figure 1d) and Extended Data Table 1
quote: uniform low noise (AP band ~5 uV root-mean-squared (RMS) Figure 1d; LFP band ~9 uV RMS
notes: Full text from PMC5955206 via NCBI BioC API. Extended Data Table 1 AP-band noise values (mean +/- SD): 5.7+/-0.8, 6.6+/-0.8, 5.5+/-0.7, 6.6+/-2.5 uV rms. Units with waveform peak >20 uV were counted as present on a site.

claim: In rat cortical slices, extracellular fields as small as 0.74 mV/mm (Ve amplitude 0.07 mV) significantly entrained spike timing at 1 Hz, whereas ~5.58 mV/mm was needed at 30 Hz; the minimal causally effective field is ~1 mV/mm and subthreshold somatic polarization stayed below 0.5 mV.

source.authors: Anastassiou CA, Perin R, Markram H, Koch C
source.title: Ephaptic coupling of cortical neurons

quote: an external field as small as 0.74 mV mm-1 (Ve amplitude of 0.07 mV)
notes: Full text read from a PDF copy hosted at gwern.net (search-result URL), not the Nature site. Introduction states endogenous fields are 'under 5 mV mm-1'; Discussion: minimal effective fields 'approximately 1 mV mm-1'.

claim: In ferret neocortical slices, applied electric fields modulate the slow oscillation with a threshold of <= 0.5 mV/mm (between 0.25 and 0.5 mV/mm); endogenous in vivo fields peak at 2-4 mV/mm (median peak 2.36 mV/mm, max 3.89 mV/mm), and 2 and 4 mV/mm fields depolarize the soma by only 0.49 and 1.29 mV.

source.authors: Fröhlich F, McCormick DA
source.title: Endogenous electric fields may guide neocortical network activity

evidence_location: Results (endogenous field measurements; constant-field intracellular recordings) and Discussion
quote: fields modulate neocortical network activity with a threshold of <= 0.5 mV/mm
notes: Full text from PMC3139922 via NCBI BioC API. Also: 'the threshold level for EF effects in vitro is between 0.25 and 0.5 mV/mm'; 'ΔVm = 0.49 +/- 0.12 mV and ΔVm = 1.29 +/- 0.20 mV, for 2 and 4 mV/mm'.

claim: Apical trunk length (soma to main bifurcation) of mouse layer 5 pyramidal neurons is 409 +/- 64 um in V1 and 313 +/- 65 um in V2m; in the 'long' (rat-derived) thick-tufted L5 model morphology the apical branch point lies 685-885 um from the soma.

source.authors: Galloni AR, Laffere A, Rancz E
source.title: Apical length governs computational diversity of layer 5 pyramidal neurons

quote: V1 mean = 409 +/- 64 um, SD, n = 22 vs V2m mean = 313 +/- 65 um
notes: Full text via NCBI BioC API (PMC7334021). These are trunk lengths, not full soma-to-tuft-tip distances; the ~1 mm soma-to-tuft figure for rat/human L5 cells (Spruston 2008) was NOT verified (see t1-22). DOI inferred from the eLife article number.

claim: Spruston (2008) review of pyramidal-neuron dendritic structure: cited as source for the ~1 mm soma-to-apical-tuft length of layer 5 pyramidal neurons, but no length figure was visible in the abstract.

source.authors: Spruston N
source.title: Pyramidal neurons: dendritic structure and synaptic integration

quote: Pyramidal neurons are characterized by their distinct apical and basal dendritic trees
notes: Paywalled full text not opened; abstract contains no numeric dendrite length. Ramaswamy & Markram 2015 (Front Cell Neurosci 9:233, open access) was also checked and gives no apical length, only basal contacts 80-120 um from soma.
